findings.text: In Luk 2:44, Joh 11:31, Joh 20:15, Act 14:19, Act 16:27 and Act 27:13 supposing is a belief about a present fact, taken up without testing: the boy is in the group, Mary goes to the tomb, the man is the gardener, Paul is dead, the prisoners have fled, the purpose is gained. The person does it, and an act rests on it.

parts.grounds: supposing him to be in the group

findings.text: The supposing leads straight into an act in the same verse: the parents travel a day and then search in Luk 2:44, the Jews follow Mary in Joh 11:31, Mary speaks to the one she takes for the gardener in Joh 20:15, the crowds drag Paul out in Act 14:19, the jailer draws his sword to kill himself in Act 16:27, the sailors weigh anchor in Act 27:13.

Where the supposing is acted on it is a pursuit of its content: in Joh 11:31 the Jews go after Mary to the tomb they suppose she goes to, in Luk 2:44 the parents go on a day's journey as if the boy were with them, in Act 27:13 the sailors sail on as if their purpose were gained.

parts.grounds: supposing that they had obtained their purpose

findings.text: What the supposing rests on is named in some verses: in Act 16:27 the jailer sees the prison doors open, in Joh 20:15 Mary is weeping and seeking the body, in Act 14:19 the crowds have stoned Paul. The supposing is taken from what is seen or felt, not from what is so.

parts.grounds: saw that the prison doors were open

findings.text: In 1Cor 8:2, 1Ti 6:5, Luk 7:43 and Joh 21:25 a view is held: that one knows something, that godliness is gain, which debtor would love more, how many books the world could hold. The person holds it as a judgment of his own.

parts.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

findings.text: In 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Jam 1:7 the view is forbidden: the king is not to suppose all his sons dead or take it to heart, and the doubter is not to suppose he will receive from the Lord.

Where the view is forbidden it is a refusal: in 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 the king is to refuse the view that all his sons are dead, and in Jam 1:7 the doubter is to refuse the expectation of receiving.

In Act 13:25, Rom 2:3 and Jam 4:5 the view is asked of the hearers: what they suppose John to be, whether the one who judges supposes he will escape God's judgment, whether the readers suppose the Scripture speaks for nothing. The question tests the view it asks about.

parts.grounds: What do you suppose that I am

findings.text: The verse tests the view and corrects or confirms it: in Act 2:15 the men are not drunk, since it is the third hour; in Act 13:25 John says he is not the one; in 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 Amnon alone is dead; in Luk 7:43 Jesus says Simon has judged rightly.

parts.grounds: For these people are not drunk, as you suppose

findings.text: In 1Cor 8:2, Rom 2:3 and Jam 1:7 the view is about oneself: that one knows, that one will escape judgment, that one will receive. Each verse sets the view against what is so: not yet knowing as one ought, God's judgment, the doubter's lack.

parts.grounds: you who judge those who practice such things

findings.text: The view is set in the heart or mind: in 2Sa 13:33 the king is not to take the report to heart, in 1Ti 6:5 the false view is held by people depraved in mind, and in Pro 18:11 the rich man's wealth is a wall in his own imagination.

parts.grounds: so take it to heart as to suppose

findings.text: In Pro 18:11 and Act 17:29 imagination is the mind's own picture or device: the rich man pictures his wealth as a high wall, and human art and imagination form an image of gold or stone. What is pictured is not the thing itself.

parts.grounds: like a high wall in his imagination

findings.text: In Act 17:29 and 1Ti 6:5 the false view is about God: the divine being is thought like an image formed by man, and godliness is taken for a way to gain. The verses deny both.

parts.grounds: we ought not to think that the divine being is like gold

findings.text: In Psa 41:7 imagining is devising harm: those who hate the psalmist plan the worst for him while they whisper together.

parts.grounds: they imagine the worst for me

findings.text: The devising of Psa 41:7 is a pursuit of harm against a person, and it comes from hatred: all who hate the psalmist whisper and plan the worst against him.

parts.grounds: All who hate me whisper together about me

findings.text: In Gen 18:28 to Gen 18:32 suppose is a particle that puts a case, not an act of the mind: Abraham puts lower numbers of righteous one after another, asks the Lord not to be angry, and each case is answered by the Lord's not destroying. In Eze 18:14 the prophet puts the case of a son who sees his father's sins and does not do them.
